text:
marcus: Heads-up, found an advisory referencing a local privilege escalation in the nvidia kernel module affecting 525.x/530.x families. CVE-2026-XXXX. Can we quickly scope impact for Redwood Dedicated + Private images?

olga: thanks. do we know which of our images ship the affected driver? I think some private clusters pinned 525.85 and some dedicated pools on 530.41.

jamie: i ran a quick query against image metadata: `grep -R "nvidia-driver" /images/metadata || true` — looks like private/v1.12 uses 525.85, dedicated/pool-alpha uses 530.41. adding the exact locations in the infra ticket.

marcus: good. immediate questions: (1) is there an available signed KMS-signed driver package we can push, (2) any kernel ABI break between 525 and 530 that will block fast patching, (3) can we do a non-disruptive rollout for private?

olga: on KMS: vendor published signed RPMs but our KMS signing verification fails on some images — need to confirm our attestation path. @cloud-ops can you confirm whether the image build pipeline validates signed driver artifacts with our KMS key?

cloud-ops: checking — the image-builder job calls `kms-verify --key projects/redwood-kms/keys/nvsign` as part of publishing. but older AMIs (pre-2024-08) used an ephemeral key. i can enumerate which AMIs skip verification.

jamie: kernel ABI: there are a few symbol changes between 525 -> 530 but we have kernel-5.15 and kernel-6.1 families in prod. 525 on 5.15 is fine, 530 on 6.1 is expected. the main risk is mixing a 530 driver with a 5.15 kernel — will fail to load. so for private we need per-image builds not a single blob replacement.

olga: OK that means two parallel tracks: (A) sign+publish vendor hotpatches for the matching driver/kernel combinations, (B) plan per-image rebuilds where verification fails. Prioritization: Dedicated pools running customer-facing low-latency endpoints should be highest.

marcus: agreed. also need to surface RBAC change: only infra-release role should be able to publish signed driver artifacts. can we add a short-lived policy today?

cloud-ops: i can add a temporary IAM condition: `roles/infra-release` allowed to call `kms.asymmetricSign` for `nvsign` key. will push change, but will need approval from sec@redwood for prod key change.

sre-bot: deploy-ci: image-builder/verify-nvsign — 1 failure (ami-0a12bb...), see: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234/artifacts/verify.log

jamie: thanks. i grabbed the failing AMI log: error `KMS_VERIFY: key mismatch: signed-by=vendor-key-v1 vs expected=nvsign`. that AMI was built by an old pipeline. recommend rebuild and re-verify.

olga: risk classification: local privilege escalation that requires module load and local access. impact: moderate-high for Dedicated where developers/admins can ssh into GPUs. For Private (customer-managed network) risk depends on customer isolation.

marcus: propose schedule: emergency fast patch for Dedicated canary pool tonight 02:00 UTC (low traffic), full Dedicated sweep tomorrow 03:00-07:00 UTC, private image rebuilds staged over 72h. canary test will validate driver load + end-to-end inference smoke test. thoughts?

jamie: +1. for canary we should run the following smoke test (adds both functional and perf sanity):
```
# smoke test
modinfo nvidia | grep -E 'version:|pci_device'
python -c "from inference_client import Client; c=Client(); print(c.generate('hello', model='gpt-small'))"
# run 30s perf warmup and check  p99 < 450ms
./perf-run --duration 30 --target p99
```

cloud-ops: allocating `gpu-dedicated-canary-1` pool for tonight. will snapshot current AMIs and create rollback tags.

olga: we should also add audit logging to capture `insmod/rmmod` and `modprobe` events on GPU nodes for the next 7 days. that will help detect exploitation attempts. @marcus can you open a quick infra ticket?

marcus: opened: https://infra.internal/tickets/RED-9842 — includes checklist: identify AMIs, build signed packages, schedule canary, RBAC change, audit logging, incident comms.

sre-bot: incident-tracker: RED-9842 created by marcus at 1945678923

jamie: final note — NCCL/cuDNN/CUDA compatibility: ensure we pick driver builds that match the CUDA minor versions we ship. i.e., driver 525.x -> CUDA 11.8, 530.x -> CUDA 12.1. we'll need test matrix across both. i'll open a matrix PR to infra-tests repo.

olga: assigning owners: jamie -> test matrix + smoke scripts, cloud-ops -> build/verify pipeline changes + IAM update, marcus -> canary schedule + comms, olga -> triage & severity decision. target: canary tonight.

marcus: thanks everyone. i'll post a short status update in #incidents and ping core-ops before kickoff. :white_check_mark:
